🇲🇽📈 22.78 MILLION JOBS: MEXICO'S FORMAL EMPLOYMENT RECORD

Mexico just hit an all-time high in formal employment: 22.78 million jobs registered with the IMSS, 454,000 more than a year ago, with the base contribution wage up 6.4% — beating inflation. Per the OECD's 2026 report, Mexico now has the second-lowest unemployment rate among all 38 member countries, behind only Japan. (El Economista / IMSS data)

🇲🇽⚡ MOODY'S REAFFIRMS CFE'S TOP RATING — AAA.mx

They said state ownership would sink it. Moody's just reaffirmed CFE's top rating — AAA.mx, the highest on the Mexican scale — citing the public utility's "strategic role" and its ~72% share of national power generation. The company neoliberals spent decades trying to break up and sell off is now a benchmark for creditworthiness in Mexico.

🚨🇲🇽 MEXICO'S AG: US GAVE FALSE DATA ON THE ZAMBADA FLIGHT

Mexico's Attorney General Ernestina Godoy said it plainly: US authorities "repeatedly gave false or imprecise data" about the plane that flew Mayo Zambada out of Mexico in 2024. The FGR found the takeoff runway had no operating permit, the aircraft's ID markers altered, and audio of the pilot asking the Ciudad Juárez tower for a transponder code. Ambassador Salazar had sworn Washington was not involved. The case is reopened.

🔥🇲🇽 PAN GOVERNOR ADMITTED THE FOREIGN AGENTS WERE CIA

A sitting Mexican governor confirmed on camera that the foreign agents operating in her state were CIA. Morena's Ariadna Montiel says Chihuahua's PAN governor Maru Campos didn't just permit it — she "executed, shared and agreed" to US intelligence operating on Mexican soil, no laws respected. Chihuahuenses are already collecting signatures to recall her.

🇲🇽💰 NO INHERITANCE TAX: SHEINBAUM SHUTS IT DOWN

No inheritance tax in Mexico. Sheinbaum killed the idea flat — "we don't believe inheritances should be taxed" — and Morena's Ricardo Monreal confirmed zero new taxes in the 2027 economic package. The 4T has funded record social spending by making big taxpayers pay what they already owed through SAT enforcement, not by inventing new levies on working families.

🚨🇲🇽 US RETURNS MEXICO'S ICE PROTEST LETTERS — UNOPENED

Washington just mailed Mexico's protest letters back over 18 dead migrants. State Dept's Michael Kozak told Ambassador Lazzeri the notes "purport to direct the actions of U.S. Government personnel operating in U.S. sovereign territory," and to use "diplomatic channels." The letters were a cease-and-desist to the private contractor running the detention center where Lorenzo Salgado was killed on July 7 in Houston. Mexico takes note — and keeps the demand on the table.

FOX NEWS: Inside look at the dangerous cartel smuggling tunnels still being used at border

July 17, 2026 | 🔴

Fox's "exclusive" underground tour of El Paso storm drains — "32 entry points," smugglers charging "$20,000–$30,000." Then, buried in its own copy: "With crossings down… smugglers are now moving smaller groups."

Crossings at record lows, yet the segment sells a border "still" being overrun. Fox's own data undercuts Fox's own fear.

• "you're already exhausted, and now you have to potentially fight with someone underground"
• Fox's own line: "With crossings down, Border Patrol says smugglers are now moving smaller groups"

TEXAS TRIBUNE: Drifting anti-immigrant buoys briefly close 2 Rio Grande bridges

July 17, 2026 | 🟢

100+ federal border buoys broke loose in the flooded Rio Grande and drifted toward Eagle Pass — closing two international bridges (~9,000 vehicles/day) for hours.

CBP swore "Operation River Wall" — 500+ miles of buoy barriers — could survive a 100-year flood. It didn't survive one July storm. The barrier built to stop people ended up stopping legal cross-border trade.

• CBP said the system was "engineered to withstand a 100-year flood"
• ~9,000 vehicles cross the two shuttered bridges daily

REUTERS: The economic goal that never came — World Cup falls short of boosting Mexico

July 17, 2026 | 🟡

Reuters: the World Cup added about $2B to Mexico — 0.1% of GDP, and less than half the $5.6B Mexico received in remittances in May alone.

The same piece names the real drag: not the tournament, but USMCA uncertainty and weak investment — i.e. Trump's trade threats, not Mexico's hosting.

• "The World Cup will not structurally change the trajectory of the Mexican economy" — Rankia chief economist
• Banamex: total impact ~$2 billion, about 0.1% of GDP

USA TODAY: Mexico's president accepting Trump's invitation to attend World Cup final

July 18, 2026 | 🟢

Sheinbaum says she got a "direct invitation" from Trump to Sunday's final at MetLife — her first face-to-face with him since December's draw. US outlets frame it as a diplomatic reset.

After a month of DEA "cartel" accusations and disputes over Mexicans killed in ICE custody, the two share a VIP box. Cooperation and confrontation running on parallel tracks.

• Sheinbaum: received a "direct invitation" from Trump
• Bloomberg: the final draws the three leaders "for first meeting since December"
